column21: What did you like most about Tab Time, and what could be improved in future versions?
The donut chart in the popup gave me an instant reality check on how my quick 5-minute Twitter breaks were quietly adding up to over 40 minutes. It completely changed how I pace my study sessions.
Seeing the exact time spent per academic journal on ScienceDirect helped me organize my literature review. Extremely clean UI and zero lag.

Knowing that every single byte of my browsing data stays right here on my laptop with no cloud server accounts gave me complete peace of mind. I refused to use RescueTime due to privacy, but Tab Time is fantastic.
Focus Mode holding page is polite but firm. It effectively interrupted my mindless tab-opening habit when studying for finals.
Would love to see custom sub-page categorization (e.g., separating YouTube educational tutorials from entertainment channels) in a future update.
Super lightweight! Even with 25+ tabs open across two monitors, there was no noticeable browser stutter or memory drain.
The daily productivity score became a personal game for me. I tried to keep my score above 80% every workday.
I appreciate that there are no annoying pop-up notifications during deep work sessions. The non-intrusive design is refreshing.
A dark mode toggle for the full dashboard would make it even better for late-night research sessions.
The 60-second idle detection is very accurate. It didn't inflate my hours when I stepped away to grab a coffee.
Great tool for keeping myself accountable while working remotely from home. Simple, fast, and does exactly what it promises.
Being able to edit domain categories easily from the settings page saved me a lot of time for niche development tools.
The countdown timer on the focus holding page gives just enough friction to stop habitual social media checking.
I found the weekly bar chart very insightful for seeing which days of the week I procrastinate the most.
Adding an optional sound chime when a focus session concludes would be a great addition to the Pomodoro workflow.
Much better than StayFocusd because it provides detailed analytics rather than just a harsh blocking wall.
Very easy to install and get started. Didn't need to read any instructions or manuals.
Helped me manage my ADHD-related hyper-focus on unrelated rabbit holes during my dissertation writing.
I like the one-click focus start from the toolbar. It creates an intentional boundary before I start coding.
Data export as JSON worked seamlessly when I wanted to backup my weekly logs.
The category breakdown by color is very intuitive. You can understand your day in less than 2 seconds.
